case_name: L. O. v. Mt. Lebanon S.D.

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the District’s appeal from the common pleas order was timely and properly taken.

issues.label: Finality of order reviewed
issues.why: The court must determine whether the common pleas order is final/appealable and what agency action is under review (the Board adjudication).

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct scope/standard for reviewing a school board residency adjudication as modified (or not) by common pleas.

issues.label: Common pleas review scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether common pleas acted within its review authority (record review vs de novo factfinding) in a Local Agency Law appeal.

issues.label: Whether record closed on appeal
issues.why: The court must determine whether additional materials (e.g., supplemental reproduced record) were properly excluded/considered after the court ruled the certified record complete.

issues.label: Judicial notice of policy
issues.why: The court must decide if the District’s Residency/Enrollment Policy is a proper subject of judicial notice and whether it can be considered if not in the certified record.

issues.label: Preservation and waiver
issues.why: The court must determine which arguments were preserved below and which are waived for being raised first on appeal.

issues.label: Issue framing and forfeiture
issues.why: The court must identify the precise issues decided by the Board and common pleas and ensure parties are not changing theories mid-appeal.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must decide who bears the burden to prove residency/non-residency under Section 1302(a) and applicable precedent and when (if ever) any burden shifts.

issues.label: Quantum of proof required
issues.why: The court must identify the correct evidentiary standard (e.g., substantial evidence supporting the agency; preponderance in the hearing) governing residency determinations.

issues.label: Substantial evidence support
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board’s non-residency finding is supported by substantial evidence in the record.

issues.label: Errors of law by Board
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board misinterpreted Section 1302(a) or applied an incorrect legal test for “residence.”

issues.label: Errors of law by common pleas
issues.why: The court must decide whether common pleas used an incorrect legal definition of residency or otherwise committed legal error.

issues.label: Definition of student residence
issues.why: The court must determine the legal meaning of “reside” for school attendance purposes under Section 1302(a) (physical presence, intent, domicile distinctions).

issues.label: Physical presence requirement
issues.why: The court must decide what level of physical presence is legally sufficient to constitute residence for enrollment.

issues.label: Intent to remain relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how intent to remain (or to establish a home) factors into school-residency versus domicile.

issues.label: Temporary vs bona fide residence
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mother’s apartment occupancy was bona fide or merely temporary/contrived to access schools.

issues.label: Multiple residences possibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether Section 1302(a) permits a parent/child to be “resident” in more than one district simultaneously for tuition-free attendance.

issues.label: Primary residence vs dual residence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the law requires a single primary residence for school purposes or allows dual qualifying residences.

issues.label: Effect of owning Pittsburgh house
issues.why: The court must decide how continued ownership/co-ownership and use of the Pittsburgh House affects the residence analysis.

issues.label: Effect of lease and rent payments
issues.why: The court must decide the legal weight of signing a lease and paying rent when actual occupancy/access was delayed.

issues.label: Access to apartment before keys
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mother could be a resident before receiving keys/usable access and how that period affects enrollment eligibility.

issues.label: Habitability and renovations impact
issues.why: The court must decide how alleged unlivable conditions/renovations affect whether residence was established or maintained.

issues.label: One-bedroom suitability relevance
issues.why: The court must assess whether apartment size/bedroom count is relevant legally or only as circumstantial evidence of actual residence.

issues.label: Overnight-stay frequency significance
issues.why: The court must decide whether staying ~10 of 36 nights can establish residence and what legal threshold (if any) applies.

issues.label: Daytime presence vs overnight
issues.why: The court must decide whether residence depends on overnight sleeping patterns or broader living patterns (meals, belongings, daily routines).

issues.label: Mail return/vacancy evidence weight
issues.why: The court must decide the probative value of returned mail labeled “vacant” and Mother’s explanation for it.

issues.label: Utility usage evidence weight
issues.why: The court must decide the probative value of minimal electricity usage and whether it supports non-residency.

issues.label: Mailing address on electric bill
issues.why: The court must decide what inference to draw from listing the Pittsburgh House as the billing/mailing address for the apartment utilities.

issues.label: Driver’s license address relevance
issues.why: The court must decide the evidentiary significance of Mother’s driver’s license still listing the Pittsburgh House.

issues.label: Insurance and auto records relevance
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether renter’s/auto insurance address changes corroborate residence or are merely formalities.

issues.label: Furniture delivery and packages
issues.why: The court must decide the weight of furniture invoices and package deliveries as evidence of actual occupancy.

issues.label: Photos at apartment
issues.why: The court must decide the evidentiary value of photographs of the Children at the apartment for establishing residence.

issues.label: Security cameras evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether installing cameras meaningfully corroborates residence or only preparation.

issues.label: Surveillance methodology fairness
issues.why: The court must consider whether limited-date surveillance reasonably supports the Board’s findings or is too narrow to be reliable.

issues.label: Surveillance observations probative value
issues.why: The court must decide what inferences can be drawn from seeing the family leave/return to the Pittsburgh House on two dates.

issues.label: No interior inspection significance
issues.why: The court must consider whether lack of entry into the apartment by investigators limits the conclusions about occupancy.

issues.label: Therapist statement admissibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether the therapist’s statement (not live testimony) was admissible and what weight it may receive.

issues.label: Hearsay in administrative record
issues.why: The court must address to what extent hearsay is permissible and whether any critical findings rest solely on incompetent evidence.

issues.label: Credibility determinations deference
issues.why: The court must decide the level of deference owed to the Board/Hearing Officer’s credibility findings versus common pleas’ reassessment.

issues.label: Common pleas credibility reweighing
issues.why: The court must determine whether common pleas improperly substituted its view of credibility for the Board’s without a proper basis.

issues.label: Internal inconsistency in testimony
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether Mother’s and Service Provider’s inconsistent timelines undermine credibility and support the Board’s findings.

issues.label: Evasiveness as credibility factor
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board properly relied on Mother’s inability to quantify nights as a credibility basis.

issues.label: Legal relevance of motive to move
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mother’s dissatisfaction with prior district or desire for District services is legally relevant or impermissible bias evidence.

issues.label: Special-needs considerations
issues.why: The court must ensure the residency decision is not improperly influenced by the Children’s special education/service needs while recognizing relevant factual context.

issues.label: Separated parents analysis
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board erred in concluding the case does not involve separated parents and whether that affects residency rules.

issues.label: Domestic violence constraints
issues.why: The court must consider whether DV-related constraints on selling/leaving the Pittsburgh House affect the reasonableness of maintaining ties there in residency analysis.

issues.label: Parent residence vs child residence
issues.why: The court must apply the statutory rule tying the child’s school district to the parent/guardian’s residence and determine whose residence controls.

issues.label: Potential change of residence midyear
issues.why: The court must decide whether residency can change during the school year and how that affects entitlement and tuition liability.

issues.label: Tuition period and calculation
issues.why: The court must decide whether imposing tuition for the entire 2024-25 year was lawful/unsupported if residency status could change after the hearing.

issues.label: Remedy if partial-year nonresident
issues.why: The court must decide the proper remedy if the family was nonresident for part of the year but later became resident (e.g., prorated tuition, effective date).

issues.label: Effective date of residency determination
issues.why: The court must determine the relevant date(s) for assessing residency (enrollment date, investigation date, hearing date, board decision date).

issues.label: Notice and due process adequacy
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mother received adequate notice of the investigation/hearing and a meaningful opportunity to be heard.

issues.label: Policy-based 60-day notice claim
issues.why: The court must decide whether District policy required 60 school days’ notice/opportunity to establish residency and the legal effect of any violation.

issues.label: Enforceability of district policy
issues.why: The court must determine whether internal policies create enforceable rights in this adjudication and whether noncompliance warrants reversal.

issues.label: Consistency with Section 1302
issues.why: The court must ensure the District’s policies and procedures are consistent with Section 1302(a) and not ultra vires.

issues.label: Independence of hearing officer
issues.why: The court must confirm the hearing was conducted by an impartial decisionmaker consistent with administrative due process.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings and reasoning
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board adjudication includes necessary findings of fact, credibility resolutions, and legal conclusions to permit review.

issues.label: Mischaracterization of evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether either tribunal materially misread the record (e.g., “10 nights equals one-third” framing) affecting legal conclusions.

issues.label: Arbitrary/capricious considerations
issues.why: The court must assess whether the adjudication reflects reasoned decisionmaking rather than speculation or improper factors.

issues.label: After-discovered evidence motion
issues.why: The court must address whether denying the District’s request to present after-discovered video evidence was correct under the governing standard.

issues.label: Record supplementation standards
issues.why: The court must decide what showing is required to reopen the record in a local agency appeal (due diligence, materiality, noncumulative).

issues.label: Prejudice from excluding new evidence
issues.why: The court must consider whether exclusion of alleged video surveillance evidence affected substantial rights or was harmless.

issues.label: Procedural irregularities below
issues.why: The court must determine whether any procedural defects in the investigation/hearing/appeal process require remand or reversal.

issues.label: Relief and disposition options
issues.why: The court must decide the appropriate appellate remedy (reinstate Board, affirm common pleas, remand for findings, remand for new hearing, modify tuition).

issues.label: Attorney fees/costs authority
issues.why: The court must consider whether any statute/policy authorizes fees or costs related to residency enforcement and appeals (if requested or implicated).

issues.label: Equal protection/constitutional limits
issues.why: The court must consider any constitutional constraints implicated by residency enforcement (even if not heavily developed), such as arbitrary classification or denial of education without due process.

issues.label: Privacy and surveillance legality
issues.why: The court must consider whether the manner of surveillance/photography raises legal issues affecting admissibility or fairness (to the extent preserved/argued).
